# Chiptunes

> Chiptunes (https://chiptunes.studio) is a free 8-bit music tracker that runs in the browser. Songs use three pulse-wave channels and one noise channel. This file explains a plain-text song format so you can write songs for people, who then open them in Chiptunes to listen, edit and share.

## Giving the user a song

There are two ways to hand over a song. Offer the link when you can, and always include the text as well.

1. **A link** they can click: `https://chiptunes.studio/share#t1.` followed by the song text with every line break replaced by `;` and every space replaced by `_`. Leave out comment lines. Links open straight into a player with the song. Example:

   https://chiptunes.studio/share#t1.chiptunes_1;title:_Tiny;bpm:_120;pattern_A;00_C-4_50_08;04_E-4_--_--;08_G-4_--_--;12_OFF_--_--;order:_A

2. **The text itself**, in a code block. The user pastes it into Chiptunes using "Import from text" on the home page. This works for songs of any length.

If something is wrong, Chiptunes lists each problem with its line number, and the user may paste those back to you to fix.

## The format

```
chiptunes 1
title: Song name
bpm: 120

pattern Intro
# row  ch1 (note duty vol) | ch2 | ch3 | noise (rate vol)
00  C-4 50 08 | .         | C-2 50 08 | 05 08
04  E-4 -- 06 | G-3 12 03 | .         | 30 07

pattern Chorus
00  ...

order: Intro, Chorus, Chorus
```

- `chiptunes 1`: the format version. Put it first.
- `title:` the song's name. `bpm:` the tempo, a whole number from 60 to 300.
- `pattern <name>`: starts a pattern. Every pattern is exactly 64 rows, numbered `00` to `63`.
- Row lines: a row number, then the four channels in order (ch1, ch2, ch3, noise). Only write rows where something changes; rows you leave out change nothing.
  - Each channel is either `.` (nothing new) or its values: three for a pulse channel (`note duty volume`), two for noise (`rate volume`).
  - Channels left off the end of a row count as `.`.
  - The `|` separators are optional and only there for readability.
- `order:` the patterns to play, comma-separated, in sequence. Patterns can repeat. If you leave it out, every pattern plays once in the order written.
- A line starting with `#` is a comment.

### Values

- **note:** pitch `A`–`G`, then `-` (natural), `#` (sharp) or `b` (flat), then octave `2`–`7`. For example `C-4`, `F#3`, `Bb5`. `C-4` is middle C. Also `OFF` (silence the channel) and `---` (no change).
- **duty** (pulse channels only, sets the tone): `12` thin and nasal, `25` bright, `50` full square wave, `75` (sounds like 25), or `--` for no change.
- **volume:** `00` (silent) to `15` (loudest), or `--` for no change.
- **rate** (noise only): `00`–`99`, the speed of the noise. `10` is normal speed. Low values rumble, high values hiss. `--` for no change.

## How the sound works (read this before writing)

These rules decide whether a song sounds good:

1. **Time:** 4 rows make one beat, 16 rows make one bar, so a pattern is 4 bars. At 120 bpm one row lasts 1/8 of a second.
2. **Everything carries over.** A note keeps sounding until the next note or `OFF` on that channel. Volume and duty stay as last set. Each channel starts silent with volume 0, so **the first note on every channel needs a volume**.
3. **Set the volume at the start of every pattern** you use on a channel, because patterns can be played in any order.
4. **There are no envelopes.** A note stays at one volume until you change it. For plucky or fading notes, step the volume down over the following rows (for example `08`, then `05`, then `02`).
5. **Repeating the same pitch doesn't restart the note.** To hear the same pitch twice in a row, change the volume on the second one, or put `OFF` just before it.
6. **Noise plays all the time** while its volume is above 0, so drums are short bursts that you turn back down:
   - kick: rate `03`–`05`, volume `08`, then `04`, then `00` over the next rows
   - snare: rate `25`–`35`, volume `07`, then `04`, then `00`
   - hi-hat: rate `90`–`99`, volume `02` or `03` for one row, then `00`
7. **Keep the mix balanced.** All four channels add together. Good levels are a lead around `06`–`08`, harmony `03`–`05`, bass `06`–`08`, and drums `02`–`08`. Avoid going above `10`.
8. **Give each channel its own job**, for example lead melody, harmony or arpeggios, bass, and drums. Use different duty values so they're easy to tell apart.

## Example

A complete song in C major with a lead, quiet harmony, an octave-jumping bass and a simple drum beat:

```
chiptunes 1
title: Sunny Path
bpm: 140

pattern Verse
# row  lead (ch1)  | harmony   | bass      | drums
00  E-5 25 07 | C-4 12 03 | C-2 50 08 | 05 08
01  .         | .         | --- -- 05 | -- 04
02  --- -- 06 | .         | C-3 -- 08 | 99 02
03  .         | .         | --- -- 05 | -- 00
04  D-5 -- 07 | E-4 -- 03 | C-2 -- 08 | 30 07
05  .         | .         | --- -- 05 | -- 04
```
